floor_history.headline: Recon: found exact SOTN precedent (cres.c) + mapped 4 BB2 struct offsets; identified real outer-guard divergence as the frontier

s3 structural: re-verified s2 floor (136), improved to 130 via inlined base-address expr, and CONFIRMED H4's pass attribution (combine.c fold blocked by shared SS_SCORE_FLAG re-derivation liveness) vi

frontier.hypothesis: Caching the shifted bank pointer explicitly (a single s32 *bank_ptr computed once) and having all 4 SS_SCORE_FLAG-equivalent clear sites dereference it, instead of each independently re-invoking the SS_SCORE_FLAG(a0,a1) macro (which re-derives (a0<<16)>>14 from scratch every time), may let combine.c's fold window see a single-consumer intermediate and fuse the top-level shift to 2 insns - genuinely untested this session.
frontier.mechanism: combine.c local 2-3-insn fold window (confirmed this session via the .combine dump) - fold succeeds only when the intermediate value dies at the fold point
frontier.next_probe: Write and sandbox-measure a variant that caches *(s32*)&_ss_score[a0]-equivalent pointer once and rewrites the 4 unk90-clear sites to dereference it, while checking whether this changes the byte pattern of those sites away from H3's confirmed fresh-recompute shape (which may make it a dead end - H3 established BB2's own asm DOES re-derive fresh at those sites, not reuse a cached pointer)

frontier.hypothesis: The remaining ~13-instruction gap (213 built vs 200 target) may include diffs beyond the single bank-index-shift instruction once that lever is applied - not yet enumerated with a full instruction-by-instruction objdump diff.
frontier.next_probe: Once/if the bank_ptr-sharing lever from the frontier item above is measured (whether it succeeds or is killed), run a full objdump-vs-target diff (not just spot-checked ranges) to enumerate every remaining instruction-level difference.
